counterevidence_considered.description: All ten meadows lie along a single coastline, which could raise a spatial-dependence concern; however, each meadow occupies its own distinct named coast sector and appears on exactly one row, so this is not a repeated entry of the same independent unit and does not fall within the reviewed issue class.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: shared coastline but 10 distinct coast_sector values, one per meadow

source_refs.quoted_text:
Ten separate seagrass meadows along one coastline were mapped from aerial
imagery in 2015 and mapped again in 2025. Each meadow occupies its own named
stretch of coast, was surveyed once, and yields a single number: the percentage

evidence.description: The data description defines one row as one meadow surveyed once and names meadow_id as the independent-unit column, with an explicit statement that no meadow is measured twice.
evidence.observed_value: one row = one meadow; independent unit column = meadow_id

source_refs.quoted_text:
One row is: one seagrass meadow surveyed once, with its single decadal change in mapped area
Independent unit column: meadow_id

No meadow is measured twice and no two rows come from the same meadow, so the
values compared between the two anchoring regimes are independent observations.

evidence.description: data/input.csv contains exactly 10 data rows (lines 2-11) with 10 distinct meadow_id values SG-01 through SG-10 and 10 distinct coast_sector names; no independent unit appears on more than one row.
evidence.observed_value: 10 rows, 10 unique meadow_id values, 10 unique coast_sector values

evidence.description: The workflow enforces uniqueness of the independent-unit column, raising an error if any meadow_id appears on more than one row, so a repeated unit could not silently enter the test.

source_refs.quoted_text:
if len(set(labels)) != len(labels):
        raise ValueError("every meadow must appear on exactly one row")

evidence.description: split_by_regime appends exactly one response value per record to exactly one regime group, so each independent unit enters the Mann-Whitney U test exactly once; no row duplication, expansion, or repeated-measure pooling occurs anywhere in the workflow.
evidence.observed_value: one appended value per row; groups of size 5 and 5

evidence.description: Independent recomputation from the 10 CSV rows reproduces the reported statistics exactly: protected-group ranks {4,7,8,9,10} give rank sum 38, U = 38 - 15 = 23; exact two-sided p = 2*(4/252) = 0.0317; rank-biserial = 2*23/25 - 1 = 0.840; medians +7.6% and -6.8%. This confirms each of the 10 units contributed exactly one value to the test reported.

source_refs.quoted_text:
- U statistic (no-anchoring zones) = 23.0
- Exact two-sided p-value = 0.0317
- Rank-biserial correlation = 0.840

- Meadows analysed: 10
- No-anchoring zones: 5 (median extent change 7.60 %)
- Open-access meadows: 5 (median extent change -6.80 %)

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to demonstrate the issue by (1) scanning all 10 CSV data rows for repeated meadow_id or coast_sector values (none: SG-01..SG-10 and 10 distinct sector names are all unique); (2) searching the workflow for any step that could enter a unit more than once, such as row duplication, joins, per-year expansion of the 2015/2025 measurements, or bootstrap-style resampling (none exists; the paired-year design is already collapsed to one change value per meadow before the data arrive, and the code additionally raises an error on duplicate meadow_id); and (3) recomputing the Mann-Whitney U statistic and exact p-value by hand from the 10 rows, obtaining U = 23 and p = 0.0317, identical to the report, which is only consistent with each independent unit contributing exactly one observation. All attempts to falsify the no-issue conclusion failed.
